lessons.title: Describing nouns with verbs
lessons.explanation: Use ~는 것 to turn a verb phrase into a noun-like expression, such as ‘the act of studying’ or ‘the thing that I like’. This lesson is the foundation for the next several lessons.

cards.translation: The food I ate
cards.explanation: Turns a verb clause into a noun-like expression with 것, often meaning the thing or action that someone does, wants or likes. In this sentence, “먹은” completes the blank in “제가 먹은 음식” and gives it the meaning “The food I ate”. Use a verb in the present modifier form ~는 before 것. Add the past or future modifier forms before 것 when the time reference requires them.

In this sentence, “먹을” completes the blank in “내가 먹을 음식” and gives it the meaning “The food I will eat”. Use a verb in the present modifier form ~는 before 것. Add the past or future modifier forms before 것 when the time reference requires them.

lessons.title: Lesson 27: Using ~던/었던 to Describe Past Tense
lessons.explanation: Use ~던 for a remembered repeated or continuing past action and ~았/었던 for a remembered action or state that has finished. The neutral ~ㄴ/은 form is a comparison, not the target of this lesson.

cards.translation: That is the computer I had used last year
cards.explanation: ~던 and ~았/었던 describe a noun from the speaker's remembered experience. ~던 commonly presents a repeated past action that continued up to the relevant time; ~았/었던 presents a past action or state as finished and no longer continuing. The ordinary past modifier ~ㄴ/은 is the neutral comparison form. In this sentence, “썼던” completes the blank in “그 컴퓨터는 작년에 썼던 거예요” and gives it the meaning “That is the computer I had used last year”. Put the verb or adjective before the noun (or 것). For verbs, attach ~던 to the stem for the remembered/repeated or continuing sense: 입다 → 입던. For a finished remembered event or state, insert the past form before 던: 입다 → 입었던, 예쁘다 → 예뻤던. Do not use the neutral ~ㄴ/은 examples as target answers for this lesson.

The ordinary past modifier ~ㄴ/은 is the neutral comparison form. In this sentence, “썼던” completes the blank in “저는 애기가 썼던 휴지를 다 버렸어요” and gives it the meaning “I threw out all the tissue paper that the baby had used”. Put the verb or adjective before the noun (or 것). For verbs, attach ~던 to the stem for the remembered/repeated or continuing sense: 입다 → 입던. For a finished remembered event or state, insert the past form before 던: 입다 → 입었던, 예쁘다 → 예뻤던. Do not use the neutral ~ㄴ/은 examples as target answers for this lesson.

lessons.source_title: Lesson 27: Using ~던/었던 to Describe Past Tense
lessons.meaning: ~던 and ~았/었던 describe a noun from the speaker's remembered experience. ~던 commonly presents a repeated past action that continued up to the relevant time; ~았/었던 presents a past action or state as finished and no longer continuing. The ordinary past modifier ~ㄴ/은 is the neutral comparison form.
lessons.when_to_use: Use ~던 when you recall something that happened repeatedly or was continuing. Use ~았/었던 when you recall something that happened before but has ended or is no longer true. The difference is a nuance of memory and completion, so the context matters.
lessons.how_to_build: Put the verb or adjective before the noun (or 것). For verbs, attach ~던 to the stem for the remembered/repeated or continuing sense: 입다 → 입던. For a finished remembered event or state, insert the past form before 던: 입다 → 입었던, 예쁘다 → 예뻤던. Do not use the neutral ~ㄴ/은 examples as target answers for this lesson.

lessons.title: More uses of ~는 것
lessons.explanation: Build on ~는 것 with irregular verbs, preference expressions, and common noun-like constructions. Pay attention to how the form combines with 이다 and particles.

cards.translation: I saw my friend opening the door
cards.explanation: The lesson develops further uses of ~는 것, including irregular forms, preferences and situations where an action is treated as a noun. In this sentence, “여는 것” completes the blank in “저는 친구가 문을 여는 것을 봤어요” and gives it the meaning “I saw my friend opening the door”. Build the noun expression with the correct present modifier before 것; apply the irregular stem changes and particles shown in the lesson.

Build the noun expression with the correct present modifier before 것; apply the irregular stem changes and particles shown in the lesson.

Build the noun expression with the correct present modifier before 것; apply the irregular stem changes and particles shown in the lesson.

In this sentence, “사는” completes the blank in “농장에서 사는 게 싫어요” and gives it the meaning “I don’t like living on a farm”. lessons.title: Nominalizing with ~기 and ~ㅁ/음
lessons.explanation: Use ~기 and ~ㅁ/음 to turn verbs and adjectives into nouns. These forms overlap with ~는 것 but have different common patterns and registers.

cards.prompt: 쌀을 물에 넣은 후에 쌀의 색깔이 ___ 시작했어요
cards.translation: After I put the rice in the water, the color of the rice started to change
cards.explanation: ~기 and ~ㅁ/음 nominalize verbs and adjectives. HTSK compares these noun forms with the earlier ~는 것 construction. In this sentence, “변하기” completes the blank in “쌀을 물에 넣은 후에 쌀의 색깔이 변하기 시작했어요” and gives it the meaning “After I put the rice in the water, the color of the rice started to change”. Attach ~기 to the stem, or form the appropriate ~ㅁ/음 ending from the stem; then add particles or following predicates.

In this sentence, “먹기” completes the blank in “밥을 먹기 싫어” and gives it the meaning “I don’t want to eat”. Attach ~기 to the stem, or form the appropriate ~ㅁ/음 ending from the stem; then add particles or following predicates.

Attach ~기 to the stem, or form the appropriate ~ㅁ/음 ending from the stem; then add particles or following predicates.

In this sentence, “달리기를” completes the blank in “저는 달리기를 할 거예요” and gives it the meaning “I will go for a run”. Attach ~기 to the stem, or form the appropriate ~ㅁ/음 ending from the stem; then add particles or following predicates.

cards.translation: I’m bad at skipping
cards.explanation: ~기 and ~ㅁ/음 nominalize verbs and adjectives. HTSK compares these noun forms with the earlier ~는 것 construction. In this sentence, “줄넘기를” completes the blank in “저는 줄넘기를 못해요” and gives it the meaning “I’m bad at skipping”. Attach ~기 to the stem, or form the appropriate ~ㅁ/음 ending from the stem; then add particles or following predicates.

lessons.when_to_use: Use ~기 for many everyday noun expressions and ~ㅁ/음 for written, formal or statement-like noun forms where the lesson uses it.

lessons.title: Expressing uncertainty and duration
lessons.explanation: Use ~는지, ~(으)ㄴ지, and ~(으)ㄹ지 to express uncertainty. You will also see these forms used with 얼마나 and for actions continuing over a period of time.

cards.translation: I don’t know where my friend is going
cards.explanation: ~는지, ~(으)ㄴ지 and ~(으)ㄹ지 express uncertainty or an indirect question. ~지 can also combine with time expressions to say how long it has been. In this sentence, “가는지” completes the blank in “저는 친구가 어디 가는지 몰라요” and gives it the meaning “I don’t know where my friend is going”. Match the ending to a present action, adjective or noun, past event, or future possibility, then place the clause before 알다, 모르다 or a similar predicate.

lessons.title: ~는 것 with 이다

lessons.title: Purpose and trying
lessons.explanation: Use ~려고 and ~러 to express purpose, and ~아/어 보다 to say that you try or experience doing something.

cards.translation: I try to meet that friend every weekend
cards.explanation: ~려고 and ~러 express purpose, while ~아/어 보다 means to try an action or to have the experience of doing it. In this sentence, “만나려고” completes the blank in “그 친구를 매 주말 만나려고 노력해요” and gives it the meaning “I try to meet that friend every weekend”. Use verb stem + ~려고, or verb stem + ~(으)러 with a movement verb. Attach ~아/어 보다 to the verb stem and conjugate 보다.

cards.translation: I am trying to learn Korean
cards.explanation: ~려고 and ~러 express purpose, while ~아/어 보다 means to try an action or to have the experience of doing it. In this sentence, “배우려고” completes the blank in “한국어를 배우려고 노력하고 있어요” and gives it the meaning “I am trying to learn Korean”. Use verb stem + ~려고, or verb stem + ~(으)러 with a movement verb. Attach ~아/어 보다 to the verb stem and conjugate 보다.

cards.translation: Shall we go to the show in Seoul?
cards.explanation: ~려고 and ~러 express purpose, while ~아/어 보다 means to try an action or to have the experience of doing it. In this sentence, “보러” completes the blank in “서울에 있는 공연을 보러 갈래요?” and gives it the meaning “Shall we go to the show in Seoul?”. Use verb stem + ~려고, or verb stem + ~(으)러 with a movement verb. Attach ~아/어 보다 to the verb stem and conjugate 보다.

cards.translation: I came here to see that performance
cards.explanation: ~려고 and ~러 express purpose, while ~아/어 보다 means to try an action or to have the experience of doing it. In this sentence, “보러” completes the blank in “그 공연을 보러 여기에 왔어요” and gives it the meaning “I came here to see that performance”. Use verb stem + ~려고, or verb stem + ~(으)러 with a movement verb. Attach ~아/어 보다 to the verb stem and conjugate 보다.

cards.translation: I am going to the event to see that performance
cards.explanation: ~려고 and ~러 express purpose, while ~아/어 보다 means to try an action or to have the experience of doing it. In this sentence, “보러” completes the blank in “공연을 보러 그 행사에 가고 있어요” and gives it the meaning “I am going to the event to see that performance”. Use verb stem + ~려고, or verb stem + ~(으)러 with a movement verb. Attach ~아/어 보다 to the verb stem and conjugate 보다.

lessons.meaning: ~려고 and ~러 express purpose, while ~아/어 보다 means to try an action or to have the experience of doing it.
lessons.when_to_use: Use the purpose forms when one action is done in order to do another; use 보다 when talking about trying or experiencing an action.
lessons.how_to_build: Use verb stem + ~려고, or verb stem + ~(으)러 with a movement verb. Attach ~아/어 보다 to the verb stem and conjugate 보다.
examples: 공연을 보러 행사에 가고 있어요
I am going to the event to see the performance
공연을 보러 행사에 갈 거예요
I will go to the event to see the performance
나는 밥을 먹으려고 노력했다
I tried to eat rice
나는 밥을 먹어 봤다
I tried to eat (the) rice

lessons.title: The noun 중
lessons.explanation: Learn two common uses of 중: after a verb with ~는 것 to mean ‘in the middle of doing’, and after a group of nouns to mean ‘among’.

cards.translation: I am eating
cards.explanation: 중 means middle or among. The lesson uses ~는 중 for an action in progress and ~중에서 for choosing from a group. In this sentence, “먹는 중이야” completes the blank in “나는 먹는 중이야” and gives it the meaning “I am eating”. Use verb + ~는 중이다 for an action in progress; use noun + 중에서 for among/from a set, then add the normal predicate.

cards.translation: I am studying
cards.explanation: 중 means middle or among. The lesson uses ~는 중 for an action in progress and ~중에서 for choosing from a group. In this sentence, “공부하는 중이야” completes the blank in “나는 공부하는 중이야” and gives it the meaning “I am studying”. lessons.meaning: 중 means middle or among. The lesson uses ~는 중 for an action in progress and ~중에서 for choosing from a group.
lessons.when_to_use: Use 중 when something is currently underway or when comparing or selecting one item among several.
lessons.how_to_build: Use verb + ~는 중이다 for an action in progress; use noun + 중에서 for among/from a set, then add the normal predicate.
examples: 아저씨가 프린터를 복구하는 중이에요
The man is in the middle of repairing the printer
모든 프린터 중에 이것이 제일 싸요
Of all the printers, this one is the cheapest
나의 친구들 중에 나는 슬기를 가장 좋아해
Among my friends, I like Seulgi the most
밥과 빵 중에 밥이 더 맛있어요
